notes.meaning: God calls out to Cush, a land along the upper Nile south of Egypt. The description of whirring wings points to swarms of buzzing insects along its waterways, or perhaps the spread sails of its ships. The message begins by getting the attention of this distant and active nation as world tensions rise.

Envoys from Cush travel down the Nile in light papyrus boats to arrange an alliance against the Assyrian Empire. Isaiah tells these swift messengers to head back home to their tall, powerful people. Judah did not need to rely on foreign help, because the Lord had already decided to defend His people on His own.

The Lord calls all the people of the world to watch and listen for what He is about to do. In the ancient world, leaders raised signal flags on mountains and blew ram's horns to call armies together for war. In the same clear way, God will give an unmistakable sign to the nations when He brings down Assyria.

God tells Isaiah that He will quietly look on from His heavenly dwelling without rushing to act. Just like the steady heat of the summer sun or a quiet cloud of morning dew during harvest, the Lord remains still while human plans develop. He is untroubled by powerful armies and waits patiently for the exact right moment to step in.

Right before the harvest arrives, when grape blossoms turn into ripening fruit, God suddenly acts. He behaves like a gardener who uses a pruning knife to cut off the shoots and throw away the branches. The Assyrian invaders feel confident their conquest will succeed, but the Lord cuts their plans short just before they reach their goal.

The discarded branches represent the bodies of the fallen enemy soldiers left behind on the battlefield. There will be so many slain troops that scavenger birds will feed on them all summer and wild animals will scavenge them through the winter. This shows the complete collapse awaiting any power that sets itself against God.

After the Lord defeats the Assyrian army, the people of Cush will bring gifts of honor to the Lord of Hosts. Instead of Judah paying for an alliance, this tall and mighty African kingdom will send worship and tribute to Mount Zion in Jerusalem. This points forward to the day when foreign nations recognize the true God and bring their praise to Him.
